title: Neon Shatter
premise: A neon arcade survival game where the player taps falling geometric targets on a cyber-grid, scoring by shattering safe shapes and avoiding hazardous traps.
interaction_model: Single-screen pointer/touch input; tap falling targets directly on the canvas before they cross the bottom of the screen.
objective: Survive as long as possible and earn a high score by hitting normal and bonus targets while avoiding hazard targets and preventing safe targets from slipping past.
progression: Endless score-attack progression with gradually faster spawning and rising pressure instead of discrete levels.
theme: Futuristic neon cyberspace defense with glowing geometry, digital-grid visuals, and arcade feedback.
mood: Fast, flashy, tense, reactive, and polished with a strong arcade-mobile feel.
likely_audience: players who enjoy short-session tap games
confidence_notes: High confidence in the core loop: tap safe falling targets, avoid dangerous ones, and survive with limited lives.
High confidence that the game is endless rather than stage-based because difficulty scales continuously through spawn timing.
Moderate confidence in the fiction/theme framing; the code implies a cyber-grid stabilization fantasy but not a detailed narrative world.
recreation_prompt: Recreate a polished single-screen arcade action game called "Neon Shatter" set on a glowing sci-fi cyber grid. The player never controls a character directly; instead they interact by tapping or clicking falling geometric targets on a fullscreen canvas. Safe cyan targets are the standard objects and award 10 points when tapped. Rare golden bonus targets award 50 points and should feel valuable and exciting to hit. Red triangular hazard targets must be avoided; tapping one immediately costs a life. If any safe or bonus target falls off the bottom of the screen, the player also loses a life, but hazard targets can fall off harmlessly. Start the player with 3 lives and end the run when all lives are gone, then show a dramatic game-over overlay with the final score and a retry button. Structure the game as an endless score-attack loop with no stages: targets spawn from above with random size, position, speed, and rotation, and the spawn rate ramps up over time to increase pressure. Emphasize juicy arcade feedback: particle bursts when targets shatter, floating score text, subtle screen shake, optional haptics, responsive hit/fail/bonus/game-over audio, and small animated reaction popups for major events. Present everything with a dark neon aesthetic featuring cyan, pink, gold, and red highlights, a futuristic HUD showing score and lives, glowing line-art targets, and a mobile-friendly responsive layout with safe-area-aware UI and touch-first controls.
